title: Focaccia
subtitle: A thick, olive-oil-rich Italian flatbread with rosemary and garlic
excerpt: Focaccia is one of the most forgiving breads you can make. A long, cold rest develops flavour and the generous amount of olive oil gives it its signature crispy, golden base.
sourceNotes: Focaccia has been made in Liguria for centuries. The Genoese version, focaccia al formaggio aside, is defined by its dimpled surface, pooled olive oil, and coarse salt topping.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked slices in an airtight bag for up to 1 month. Reheat from frozen in a hot oven for 8 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: For best flavour, let the dough prove overnight in the fridge instead of 1 hour. Remove 1 hour before baking.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 200C / Gas 7. The oven must be fully preheated.

content.text: The dough is wetter than most bread doughs. Do not be tempted to add more flour. The high hydration, combined with the olive oil, is what gives focaccia its open crumb and chewy texture. You will also need 7g fast-action dried yeast and 10g fine sea salt to make the dough.

items.prepNote: plus extra for the tray and top

content.text: Mix the flour, yeast, and salt in a large bowl (keep yeast and salt on opposite sides initially). Add 375ml of warm water and half the olive oil. Mix to a shaggy dough.
Tip onto the work surface. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky. It will be stickier than standard bread dough.
Oil a large baking tray generously with olive oil. Put the dough on the tray and use your hands to stretch it to fill the tray. It may spring back: let it rest for 5 minutes, then stretch again.
Drizzle the remaining olive oil over the top. Cover with a damp cloth and leave to prove for 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Preheat the oven. Press your fingers firmly all over the dough to make deep dimples. Scatter the rosemary and garlic over the top. Press them into the dimples. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden on top and the edges are crisp. The base should sound hollow when tapped.
Cool on the tray for 10 minutes before cutting. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The dough keeps springing back and won't cover the tray.
items.cause: The gluten needs more time to relax.
items.fix: Rest the dough 10 minutes, then stretch again gently.

items.symptom: The focaccia is pale and doughy inside.
items.cause: It needed longer in the oven.
items.fix: Return to the oven for 5-minute increments until golden.

items.cause: The tray was not oiled enough before proving.
items.fix: Use more oil next time; the base fries slightly in the pan.
